photos.desc: Wyandotte Cave in Indiana is an Indiana bat priority 1 hibernaculum. Credit: R. Andrew King/USFWS
Indiana bats are known as social animals that don’t need much personal space. In fact, they’re known to cluster so tightly that 500 bats can fit within a square foot! Photo by Andrew King/USFWS.
A group of Indiana bats (Myotis sodalis) hang upside down from a cave ceiling. A group of Indiana bats (Myotis sodalis).
Sodalis Nature Preserve in Hannibal, Missouri is home to more than 168,000 endangered Indiana bats. Gates help bats live undisturbed. Photo by Courtney Celley/USFWS.
